description: Reuse an existing helper/convention instead of hand-rolling or adding a dependency
input:
Our codebase already has a `retry` helper in `utils/retry.py`, used everywhere for flaky outbound calls. It is called as a wrapper — `retry(lambda: do_thing(), attempts=3)` — and returns whatever the callable returns. Add a 3-attempt retry around the `charge_card()` call below, following existing conventions.
```python
def process_payment(order):
    resp = charge_card(order.amount)
    return resp
```
There is no repo for you to inspect — the helper's signature and calling convention are stated above, so write the change from them rather than opening `utils/retry.py`.
rubric: PASS only if the implementation reuses the existing `retry` helper rather than hand-rolling a new retry loop or pulling in a new third-party dependency.
